- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or shows negative drift, especially after recent spikes.
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment >0.8 and price rises >5% from prior day.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% if sentiment <0.6.
- Lagged bias: if forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 1–3% per day.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is consistently below 0.5 over last 7 days.
- Avoid overconfidence in sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment >0.8 but price drops >3% from prior day, reduce forecast by 3–5%.
